text: Direct-use geothermal systems skip electricity generation entirely and pipe warm water straight to where heat is needed. Towns in volcanic regions run district heating networks from wells only a few hundred metres deep, greenhouses use the water to grow vegetables through the winter, and some spas and fish farms rely on it all year. Because the water does not need to be hot enough to drive a turbine, direct use works with much cooler resources than a power plant, and the conversion losses are small.
